enzyme_name: Phytoene synthase (15-cis-phytoene synthase)
distinct_activities: lycopene beta-cyclase (EC 5.5.1.19) - fused C-terminal domain in fungi
organism_context: Plant PSY (the AraCyc/BrachyCyc RXN1F-144 context) and bacterial CrtB are stand-alone; in fungi the same phytoene synthase activity sits on a fused chain with lycopene cyclase (Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous CrtYB, Mucorales/Neurospora CarRA/AL-2).
rationale: The reaction is the head-to-head condensation of two GGPP molecules to phytoene, run by phytoene synthase; in fungi this activity is one domain of the fused bifunctional phytoene synthase/lycopene cyclase CrtYB-CarRA, while plant/bacterial orthologues are monofunctional.
direction_note: ModelSEED writes 1 GGPP <=> 1 phytoene; the real reaction consumes 2 GGPP and expels 2 diphosphate, and that PPi release makes GGPP->phytoene committed and effectively irreversible, so the enormous positive dG from the unbalanced equation is an artefact.

enzyme_name: Peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (ACOX1, straight-chain acyl-CoA oxidase)
organism_context: Mammalian peroxisome; this is the C24:6 desaturation step of the Sprecher pathway to DHA (KEGG M00861, KO K00232).
rationale: ACOX1 is a monofunctional homodimeric FAD flavo-oxidase that performs only the alpha,beta-desaturation; the bifunctional enzyme of this pathway is the next one, D-bifunctional protein HSD17B4 (hydratase + dehydrogenase), which does not catalyse this reaction.
direction_note: KEGG R07934 is written with O2 -> H2O2 (EC 1.3.3.6, an oxidase); ModelSEED substituted free FAD/FADH2, which both removes the O2 driving force and makes the step look near-equilibrium. With O2 as acceptor the dehydrogenation is irreversible.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous deformylation of AFMU to AAMU
organism_context: Human caffeine metabolism; AFMU is the NAT2 product and decomposes to AAMU in urine and in vitro.
rationale: KEGG R07941 carries the explicit COMMENT 'non enzymatic decomposition'; AFMU is a chemically labile N-formyl compound that hydrolyses to AAMU, which is why caffeine phenotyping assays quantify AFMU+AAMU together. No catalysing enzyme exists.
direction_note: The hydrolytic loss of formate is irreversible; ModelSEED's '<' would re-formylate AAMU, which neither an enzyme nor spontaneous chemistry does. The equation is also missing H2O and formate.

enzyme_name: Peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (ACOX1, straight-chain acyl-CoA oxidase)
organism_context: Mammalian peroxisome; C24:5 desaturation step of the Sprecher/VLCFA beta-oxidation route (KEGG M00861, KO K00232).
rationale: Same enzyme as rxn07724: ACOX1 is a monofunctional FAD-dependent acyl-CoA oxidase; the bifunctional protein of peroxisomal beta-oxidation (HSD17B4) acts on the product, not here.
direction_note: KEGG R07950 uses O2 -> H2O2; ModelSEED replaced the oxygen couple with free FAD/FADH2, erasing the thermodynamic driving force that makes the desaturation one-way.

enzyme_name: Enamidase (6-oxo-1,4,5,6-tetrahydronicotinate amidohydrolase, EC 3.5.2.18)
distinct_activities: hydrolysis of the enamine intermediate to (S)-2-formylglutarate + NH3
organism_context: Eubacterium barkeri (Clostridia) nicotinate fermentation cluster; homologues in other Clostridia and Proteobacteria.
rationale: Kress et al. title and characterise enamidase explicitly as 'a bifunctional enzyme of the nicotinate catabolism': a single binuclear Zn/Fe amidohydrolase-fold chain that first decyclises the lactam and then hydrolyses the resulting enamine, two chemically distinct hydrolytic steps.
direction_note: The two hydrolytic steps both sit on this one enzyme, so the 2-H2O lumped equation is legitimate; amide hydrolysis with NH3 release runs one way and the reverse (NH3 + 2-formylglutarate -> cyclic lactam) is not an activity of this enzyme.

enzyme_name: none identified - KEGG flags R08041 as an 'unclear reaction'
organism_context: Anaerobic TNT transformation (triaminotoluene -> 2,4,6-trihydroxytoluene branch of KEGG map00633).
rationale: KEGG R08041 carries no EC, no orthology and the COMMENT 'unclear reaction'; Hawari et al. found trihydroxytoluene only after heating TAT to 100 C and could detect no 13C-p-cresol from 13CH3-TNT, so no enzyme (and arguably no reaction) links these two compounds.
direction_note: KEGG draws the arrow 2,4,6-trihydroxytoluene -> p-cresol (which would agree with the LLM call), but the source itself disowns the step and the labelling experiment argues against it, so neither direction is supportable.

enzyme_name: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase of the acyclic-terpene/geraniol degradation pathway (AtuD-type)
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Atu (acyclic terpene utilization) pathway for citronellol/geraniol; no KEGG orthology is assigned to this specific step.
rationale: The chemistry is a standard alpha,beta-desaturation of a C7 branched acyl-CoA, i.e. an acyl-CoA dehydrogenase of the Atu/Liu gene clusters; ACAD-family enzymes are monofunctional homotetrameric flavoproteins, but no individual protein has been assigned to this reaction, so the identification is inferred from chemistry.
direction_note: KEGG's KGML for map00907 draws the step in the dehydrogenation direction (5-methylhex-4-enoyl-CoA -> 2,4-dienoyl-CoA, 'irreversible'), although the entry's free-text COMMENT calls it an 'enoyl-CoA reductase'; EC 1.3.99.- means the real acceptor is ETF/quinone, not free FAD/FADH2 as written.

enzyme_name: 4-Chlorobenzoyl-CoA dehalogenase (FcbB), acting on the 4-fluoro analogue
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. CBS3 / Arthrobacter sp. TM1; KEGG assigns R08118 to KO K14418 (EC 3.8.1.7).
rationale: The only hydrolytic dehalogenase known for halogenated aromatic acyl-CoAs is 4-chlorobenzoyl-CoA dehalogenase, a monofunctional crotonase-superfamily enzyme; it works with FcbA (ligase) and FcbC (thioesterase) as three separate polypeptides, not as a fusion. Activity on the fluoro substrate is assigned by KEGG orthology rather than demonstrated, hence low confidence.
direction_note: Aromatic nucleophilic substitution of halide by an active-site aspartate followed by hydrolysis of the arylate intermediate is irreversible; KEGG also marks R08118 irreversible in the 4-fluorobenzoyl-CoA -> 4-hydroxybenzoyl-CoA direction.

enzyme_name: Benzoate cis-dihydrodiol (1,2-dihydroxycyclohexa-3,5-diene-1-carboxylate) dehydrogenase, BenD/XylL (EC 1.3.1.25); partly spontaneous for the 2-fluoro diol
organism_context: Cometabolic 2-fluorobenzoate turnover in Pseudomonas sp. B13 and related benzoate degraders.
rationale: KEGG assigns only EC 1.3.1.- and no KO; the diol is the product of benzoate 1,2-dioxygenase and is normally re-aromatised by the monofunctional SDR-family dehydrogenase BenD, but because the fluorine sits on the diol carbon this particular rearomatisation also proceeds non-enzymatically with HF and CO2 loss. Enzyme identity is inferred from chemistry.
direction_note: Both KEGG and ModelSEED write this as diol <=> catechol with NAD+/NADH, CO2 and fluoride all missing; once decarboxylation and fluoride expulsion are restored the step is irreversibly diol -> catechol, as KEGG's map00364 arrow shows.

enzyme_name: Benzoate cis-dihydrodiol (1,2-dihydroxycyclohexa-3,5-diene-1-carboxylate) dehydrogenase, BenD/XylL (EC 1.3.1.25)
organism_context: 3-fluorocatechol formation during 2-/3-fluorobenzoate cometabolism in Pseudomonas sp. B13.
rationale: Here the fluorine is retained, so this is the ordinary NAD+-dependent rearomatising dehydrogenase step of the benzoate pathway, carried out by the monofunctional short-chain-dehydrogenase BenD; KEGG gives only EC 1.3.1.- with no KO, so the assignment is inferred.
direction_note: NAD+/NADH and the CO2 lost on rearomatisation are absent from the written equation; the decarboxylative rearomatisation is irreversible in the diol -> 3-fluorocatechol direction (KEGG marks it irreversible).

enzyme_name: 6-Phospho-beta-glucosidase / arbutin-6-phosphate glucohydrolase (EC 3.2.1.86)
organism_context: Enteric bacteria and lactobacilli; arbutin is taken up and phosphorylated by a PTS, then hydrolysed intracellularly by a GH1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidase.
rationale: GH1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidases are single-domain monofunctional glycoside hydrolases that release glucose-6-phosphate plus the aglycone (hydroquinone from arbutin-6-P); broad aglycone specificity is not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis with an aromatic leaving group is physiologically irreversible, and the whole point of the PTS-phosphorylation step is to trap the sugar for one-way cleavage; ModelSEED's '<' would have the cell condense G6P with hydroquinone.

enzyme_name: Long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (E. coli FadE; mammalian ACADL/ACADVL)
organism_context: E. coli fatty-acid beta-oxidation (BiGG ACOAD8f); the same step in mammalian mitochondria is run by ACADL/ACADVL.
rationale: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases are monofunctional flavoproteins carrying out only the alpha,beta-desaturation; in E. coli the multifunctional partner is FadB (hydratase/3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase/epimerase/isomerase), which catalyses the following steps, not this one. Called from well-established knowledge.
direction_note: The physiological acceptor is electron-transfer flavoprotein (ETF) feeding the quinone pool, not free FADH2; with ETF/quinone reoxidation the beta-oxidation desaturation is irreversible, so ModelSEED's reverse-only assignment is an artefact of the free-FAD stand-in.

enzyme_name: NagZ, cytoplasmic beta-N-acetylglucosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.52)
organism_context: E. coli / Pseudomonas peptidoglycan recycling; NagZ removes GlcNAc from GlcNAc-anhMurNAc-peptides imported by AmpG.
rationale: NagZ is a single-domain GH3 exo-glycosidase whose only activity is hydrolysis of the beta-1,4 GlcNAc-anhMurNAc bond; its role in AmpC induction is regulatory consequence, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Exo-glycosidase hydrolysis of the recycling intermediate is irreversible; the reverse would require NagZ to act as a glycosyl transferase onto anhydro-MurNAc-tripeptide, which it does not.

enzyme_name: L-Aspartate oxidase, NadB (EC 1.4.3.16)
organism_context: E. coli de novo NAD biosynthesis; NadB is a soluble FAD flavoprotein homologous to the succinate/fumarate reductase flavoprotein subunit.
rationale: NadB carries one catalytic activity (oxidation of L-aspartate to iminoaspartate); it uses O2 aerobically and fumarate anaerobically as acceptor, which is substrate versatility rather than a second activity.
direction_note: The BiGG model substitutes menaquinone-8 for NadB's real acceptors (O2 -> H2O2 aerobically, fumarate anaerobically), so the computed dG does not describe the real couple; in vivo the unstable iminoaspartate is consumed immediately by quinolinate synthase NadA, pulling the reaction forward.

enzyme_name: Glycolate oxidase / glycolate dehydrogenase GlcDEF complex (catalytic FAD subunit GlcD)
organism_context: E. coli glc operon; the membrane-associated glycolate-oxidising activity requires GlcD, GlcE and GlcF together.
rationale: This is a three-subunit complex of separate polypeptides (GlcD FAD catalytic subunit, GlcE FAD, GlcF Fe-S), not a fused multifunctional chain; per protocol the catalytic subunit GlcD is recorded as monofunctional.
direction_note: Glycolate oxidation is the entry step of glycolate catabolism and is drained forward by glyoxylate consumption (malate synthase GlcB in the same operon); the enzyme has no physiological role reducing glyoxylate with menaquinol.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (hydrolytic/nitrosative) deamination of GTP to XTP
organism_context: Nucleotide-pool damage chemistry; the resulting XTP is cleared by house-cleaning ITPases (RdgB/ITPA).
rationale: ModelSEED/BiGG itself names the entry 'GTP amine hydrolysis (spontaneous)'; no enzyme is known to deaminate GTP, and the existence of dedicated XTP/ITP-hydrolysing house-cleaning enzymes is the standard evidence that XTP arises non-enzymatically from GTP.
direction_note: Deamination with NH3 loss is chemically one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would have the cell aminate XTP back to GTP, for which there is no chemistry or enzyme.

enzyme_name: PagP, outer-membrane lipid A palmitoyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.251)
organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella outer membrane; an eight-stranded beta-barrel enzyme induced by PhoP/PhoQ.
rationale: PagP has one catalytic activity, palmitoyl transfer to the lipid A 2-acyl position, selected by an internal 'hydrocarbon ruler'; its ability to acylate other acceptors (e.g. phosphatidylglycerol in Klebsiella) is the same chemistry on a different acceptor, not a second activity.
direction_note: The real acyl donor is a glycerophospholipid (released as lyso-PL), not free palmitate plus loss of water as written; with the activated ester donor restored the acylation is thermodynamically downhill, so the near-zero dG that drove ModelSEED's reverse call is an artefact of the stripped donor.

enzyme_name: PagP, outer-membrane lipid A palmitoyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.251)
organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella outer membrane; same enzyme as rxn08789 acting on Kdo2-lipid A.
rationale: Single-activity beta-barrel acyltransferase; palmitoylation of Kdo2-lipid A to the hepta-acylated species is its canonical reaction.
direction_note: Same defect as rxn08789 - free palmitate stands in for the glycerophospholipid donor and the lyso-phospholipid co-product is missing, so neither the dG nor the 3-H+ stoichiometry describes the real transfer.

enzyme_name: Murein D,D-endopeptidase (MepS/Spr, MepM/YebA, MepH, MepA, PBP4/DacB, PBP7/PbpG)
organism_context: E. coli periplasm; a redundant set of at least six D,D-endopeptidases cleaves the D-Ala-mDAP 4->3 cross-link.
rationale: The dedicated space-making endopeptidases (MepS, MepM, MepH) are single-catalytic-domain peptidases; PBP4/DacB does show both D,D-carboxypeptidase and D,D-endopeptidase activity, but at one active site as broad specificity, not as two fused domains, so monofunctional is the right call for whichever enzyme runs this reaction.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of the peptide cross-link is irreversible and is a prerequisite for sacculus expansion; cross-link formation is done by a transpeptidase using the energy of a D-Ala-D-Ala bond, never by running this hydrolase backwards.

enzyme_name: MepK, murein L,D-endopeptidase cleaving mDAP-mDAP (3->3) cross-links
organism_context: E. coli periplasm; MepK is the hydrolase specific for the LD-transpeptidase-made 3->3 cross-links.
rationale: MepK is a single-domain M15-family metallopeptidase with the one cross-link-cleaving activity; it is the only E. coli enzyme shown to cleave mDAP-mDAP cross-links, and no second catalytic function is reported.
direction_note: Peptide-bond hydrolysis is irreversible; 3->3 cross-links are re-made by YcbB/LdtD transpeptidation, not by reversing this hydrolase.

enzyme_name: Proline dehydrogenase domain of proline utilization A (PutA)
organism_context: Bifunctional/trifunctional PutA in E. coli and other Gram-negatives; the activities are on separate proteins in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (PruB/PruA) and humans (PRODH/ALDH4A1). The extra N-terminal DNA-binding domain of trifunctional PutAs is a regulatory (moonlighting) role, not a third catalytic activity.
rationale: PutA is a single polypeptide carrying both the FAD-dependent PRODH domain that runs this reaction and an NAD+-dependent P5CDH domain, with a tunnel channelling P5C between them; that is two genuine catalytic activities on one chain.
direction_note: PutA's FAD is a bound prosthetic group reoxidised by the membrane quinone pool and the P5C product is channelled straight into the P5CDH domain - both pull the PRODH half irreversibly toward P5C, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call (which comes from treating FADH2 as a free, re-usable reductant) is wrong.

enzyme_name: none - one-electron autoxidation of ubiquinol-8 by O2 (the protein annotated 'quinol monooxygenase', YgiN, catalyses a different reaction)
organism_context: E. coli respiratory chain ROS leakage; YgiN was characterised as a menadiol-oxidising quinol monooxygenase, not as a superoxide-generating enzyme.
rationale: As written (quinol + 2 O2 -> quinone + 2 superoxide + 2 H+) nothing is monooxygenated, so this is quinol/semiquinone autoxidation rather than an enzymatic monooxygenase reaction; no protein is known to catalyse it, and the enzyme whose name the model borrowed (YgiN) performs a different, oxygen-incorporating oxidation.
direction_note: Physiologically the flux is quinol -> quinone + superoxide (ROS leakage kept one-way by SOD removal of O2-); nothing reduces the quinone pool with superoxide, so ModelSEED's '<' is not a real process.

enzyme_name: ArnA (PmrI), bifunctional UDP-L-Ara4N formyltransferase / UDP-GlcA oxidative decarboxylase
distinct_activities: UDP-glucuronic acid oxidative decarboxylase / dehydrogenase (C-terminal domain, EC 1.1.1.305)
organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella Ara4N-lipid A modification pathway conferring polymyxin resistance.
rationale: ArnA is one polypeptide with two separate catalytic domains - the N-terminal 10-formyl-THF-dependent transformylase that runs this reaction and an independent C-terminal NAD+-dependent UDP-GlcA decarboxylase domain.
direction_note: Both the formyl acceptor UDP-L-Ara4N and the product UDP-L-Ara4FN have been dropped, leaving only the folate half-reaction; the real transfer consumes 10-formyl-THF (i.e. the forward direction as written) and the stripped equation cannot support any meaningful dG-based direction call.

enzyme_name: L-Aspartate oxidase, NadB (EC 1.4.3.16)
organism_context: De novo NAD biosynthesis; BiGG ASPOcm/U99 variant with the aspartate couple placed in a second compartment.
rationale: Same single-activity FAD flavoprotein as rxn08167 - it only oxidises L-aspartate to iminoaspartate; the acceptor flexibility (O2 or fumarate) is not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: NadB's FAD is a bound prosthetic group reoxidised by O2 (making H2O2) or by fumarate; writing free FAD/FADH2 as a soluble couple removes the driving force, and in vivo the labile iminoaspartate is immediately pulled on by NadA.

enzyme_name: alpha-Galactosidase (EC 3.2.1.22; GH27/GH36)
organism_context: Bacterial and fungal mannan-degrading systems; alpha-galactosidase removes alpha-1,6-galactosyl side chains from galactomannan, acting alongside separate beta-mannanase and beta-mannosidase enzymes.
rationale: GH27/GH36 alpha-galactosidases are single-activity exo-glycosidases; the other mannanolytic activities needed to degrade galactomannan sit on separate proteins, so this is a multi-enzyme system rather than a multifunctional chain.
direction_note: The debranched polysaccharide co-product is missing - galactomannan is written as being wholly consumed to one galactose - which is where the ~150-370 kJ/mol 'dG' comes from; the actual glycoside hydrolysis is irreversible in the releasing direction.
